reasoning: A hybrid strategy is chosen to combine autonomous reasoning with robust external explainability tools to detect shared spurious features. Autonomous analysis ensures domain-level grounding and pattern recognition in the feature-level alignment of misclassified instances, while XAI tools provide quantitative, model-empirical attribution scores to identify features with high influence despite lack of semantic relevance. This combination improves both precision and confidence in detecting spurious correlations.

autonomous_tasks.query: Compare all misclassified instances to identify which features appear in both Instance A and Instance B, with focus on non-semantic features like workclass, education-num, and relationship.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of shared features across both instances that are common to both misclassified inputs

autonomous_tasks.query: Evaluate whether the shared features (e.g., age=53, workclass=Local-gov, marital-status=Married-civ-spouse) have semantic or domain-level plausibility in influencing the class prediction, and assess if they are spurious (i.e., correlate with outcome without meaningful relationship).
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A reasoned assessment of whether the shared features are semantically relevant or spurious based on domain knowledge

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP provides interpretable, game-theoretic feature attributions across all instances, enabling identification of high-impact features in the misclassified set. LIME and Integrated Gradients offer local and global sensitivity to feature influence, helping to validate whether shared features drive misclassification. Sensitivity analysis confirms feature impact by ablation, which is critical for detecting spurious dependency—especially when the feature is present in all instances but not semantically meaningful. Together, these tools detect shared spurious features that are both high in attribution and non-essential to the prediction.
